verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs a checkpoint when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more ... SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT changes the 1000-page default
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to specify a different default.)'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE arrived in SQLite 3.8.8 (2015-01-16), and 3.8.8.2 (2015-01-30) fixed it so that it actually truncates
verdicts.evidence: changes.html: '2015-01-16 (3.8.8) ... Added the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE option'; '2015-01-30 (3.8.8.2) Enhance sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(TRUNCATE) ... truncates the WAL file even if there is no checkpoint work'; 3.51.0 dated 2025-11-04 with 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP' (wording 'fixed it so it actually truncates' slightly overstates: fix covers the no-work case)

verdicts.claim: Only a TRUNCATE checkpoint, a journal_size_limit (default -1, meaning no limit), or the clean close of the last connection removes the excess
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA checkpoint_fullfsync (default off) makes checkpoints use F_FULLFSYNC, which only macOS supports
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default value of the checkpoint_fullfsync flag is off. Only Mac OS-X supports F_FULLFSYNC.'

verdicts.claim: Litestream tips recommend PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 ... and PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000
verdicts.evidence: tips: 'recommended to run your application with autocheckpointing disabled ... PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0;' and 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;'

verdicts.claim: Rails 7.1 (October 2023) changed its SQLite defaults to journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL and journal_size_limit=64MB, replacing -1
verdicts.evidence: BigBinary (October 31, 2023): 'journal_size_limit is now capped at 64MB ... Previously, it was set to -1'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis ... caught the WAL-reset bug on SQLite 3.51.2 in about 15 minutes; 3.51.3 ran clean (2026-08-12)
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis (August 12, 2026): 'get SQL 3.51.2 – still buggy'; 'Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; '3.51.3 comes back clean.'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). Fix in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.'; news: 3.53.0 2026-04-09 'The WAL-reset bug is fixed in this release'

verdicts.claim: SQLite's news page ... says 3.52.0 was withdrawn because some new features were not 100% compatible with prior releases
verdicts.evidence: news: 'SQLite version 3.52.0 has been withdrawn because some of the new features found in 3.52.0 are not 100% compatible with prior releases'; Antithesis: 'rolled out and rolled back a fix that broke something else'

verdicts.claim: In February 2026 Syncthing developers traced checkpoint starvation ... checkpoints are exclusive ... treat a WAL of multiple gigabytes as critical
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing forum (Feb 6, 2026): 'As checkpoints of any kind are exclusive, we're blocking our own checkpointer'; 'If the size of the WAL reaches critical levels of multiple gigabytes, we need to act.'
